Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a distinct opacity in the right apical region with associated destruction/erosion of the adjacent first and second ribs, which is the classic radiographic presentation of a Pancoast tumour (superior sulcus tumour). This diagnosis aligns with the patient's history of long-term smoking and symptoms suggestive of local invasion or paraneoplastic effects.
